Eskimo.question: The influence of the _____ language is clear
Eskimo.fact: The influence of the Chukchi language is clear.

Eskimo.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Eskimo.question: Sometimes it is regarded rather as a group belonging to the _____ branch
Eskimo.fact: The peculiarities of this language may be the result of a supposed long isolation from other Inuit and Yupik groups, and being in contact only with speakers of unrelated languages for many centuries. Because of all these factors, the classification of the Sirenik language is not settled yet: Sireniki language is sometimes regarded as a third branch of Inuit–Yupik (at least, its possibility is mentioned).

Eskimo.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Eskimo.question: Despite the ICC's 1977 decision to adopt the term _____, this has not been accepted by all or even most Yupik people
Eskimo.fact: As a result, the Canadian government usage has replaced the term Eskimo with Inuit (Inuk in singular). The ICC charter defines Inuit as including "the Inupiat, Yupik (Alaska), Inuit, Inuvialuit (Canada), Kalaallit (Greenland) and Yupik (Russia)".

Eskimo.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Eskimo.question: The four Yupik languages, by contrast, including Alutiiq (Sugpiaq), _____'ik, Naukan (Naukanski), and Siberian Yupik, are distinct languages with phonological, morphological, and lexical differences
Eskimo.fact: The four Yupik languages, by contrast, including Alutiiq (Sugpiaq), Central Alaskan Yup'ik, Naukan (Naukanski), and Siberian Yupik, are distinct languages with phonological, morphological, and lexical differences.

Eskimo.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Eskimo.question: In Siberia, about 300 of a total of 900 _____ people still learn and study the language, though it is no longer learned as a first language by children
Eskimo.fact: About 1,050 of a total Alaska population of 1,100 Siberian Yupik people in Alaska speak the language. In Siberia, about 300 of a total of 900 Siberian Yupik people still learn and study the language, though it is no longer learned as a first language by children.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: The _____ was Australian brand of portable coolers.
Esky.fact: Esky is a brand of portable coolers, originally Australian, derived from the word eskimo. The term esky is also commonly used in Australia to generically refer to portable coolers or ice boxes and is part of the Australian vernacular, in place of words like cooler or cooler box.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: The brand name was purchased from Nylex by Coleman in _____
Esky.fact: The brand name was purchased from Nylex by Coleman in 2009.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: It was made in Sydney by Malleys but did not carry their name until around _____
Esky.fact: It was made in Sydney by Malleys but did not carry their name until around 1949.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: The first (metal-cased) portable Esky appeared in _____, sized to accommodate six 26 imperial fluid ounces (740 ml) bottles of beer or soft drink, as advertised nationally
Esky.fact: The first (metal-cased) portable Esky appeared in 1952, sized to accommodate six 26 imperial fluid ounces (740 ml) bottles of beer or soft drink, as advertised nationally.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: One such brand was _____, an Australian manufacturer, previously known for domestic "tinware" — buckets, bins, cake tins and oven trays
Esky.fact: One such brand was Willow, an Australian manufacturer, previously known for domestic "tinware" — buckets, bins, cake tins and oven trays.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: Nylex started making the plastic-cased Esky in _____
Esky.fact: Nylex started making the plastic-cased Esky in 1984.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: In _____ Nylex was still defending their ownership of the Esky trademark, but by 2002 they had allowed it to lapse
Esky.fact: In 1993 Nylex was still defending their ownership of the Esky trademark, but by 2002 they had allowed it to lapse.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: Outdoor recreation company Coleman bought the Esky brands from Nylex after the company went into administration in February _____, and later that year Coleman was producing most of the Esky line in Me
Esky.fact: Outdoor recreation company Coleman bought the Esky brands from Nylex after the company went into administration in February 2009, and later that year Coleman was producing most of the Esky line in Melbourne.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: The sale was seen as symptomatic of the decline of _____-made goods due to cheaper imports
Esky.fact: The sale was seen as symptomatic of the decline of Australian-made goods due to cheaper imports.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: Many dictionaries, including the _____ and the Macquarie Dictionary, now include definitions in their publications defining it as such
Esky.fact: Many dictionaries, including the Australian National Dictionary and the Macquarie Dictionary, now include definitions in their publications defining it as such.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: Government agencies and media outlets in _____ have used the term in preference to generic alternatives
Esky.fact: Many dictionaries, including the Australian National Dictionary and the Macquarie Dictionary, now include definitions in their publications defining it as such. Government agencies and media outlets in Australia have used the term in preference to generic alternatives.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: Though not unique to _____, Australian media have widely reported on a number of high-profile incidents involving motorised eskies fitted with small motors and wheels
Esky.fact: The esky became an essential part of the beach, outdoor dining and barbecue culture that developed in Australia during the 60s and 70s. Though not unique to Australia, Australian media have widely reported on a number of high-profile incidents involving motorised eskies fitted with small motors and wheels.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: Spectators at the closing ceremony at the _____ Summer Olympics in Sydney each received a promotional pack of a small polystyrene Esky containing other items of memorabilia
Esky.fact: Spectators at the closing ceremony at the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney each received a promotional pack of a small polystyrene Esky containing other items of memorabilia.

Esky.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Esky.question: It was made in Sydney by _____ but did not carry their name until around 1949
Esky.fact: It was made in Sydney by Malleys but did not carry their name until around 1949. By 1965 "esky" (no capital E) was being used in Australian literature for such coolers, and in 1973 Malleys, owners of the tradename, acknowledged that the term had entered the vernacular and was being used for lightweight plastic imitations.

Esky.fact: The first portable Esky was designed to carry six "standard" 26 fluid ounce (740 ml) bottles as well as a triple level food section.
